question: What is the primary purpose of configuring VLANs on a switch?
choices: To increase the physical bandwidth of a switch port
To segment a single physical switch into multiple logical broadcast domains
To encrypt traffic between switches
To assign IP addresses to end devices automatically
explanation: VLANs logically segment a switch into separate broadcast domains, isolating traffic between groups of devices even though they share the same physical infrastructure.

question: When a frame is sent across an 802.1Q trunk link, what does the switch add to identify which VLAN the frame belongs to?
choices: A source MAC address
A VLAN tag in the Ethernet frame header
An IP TTL value
A DSCP marking
explanation: 802.1Q trunking inserts a 4-byte VLAN tag into the Ethernet frame header that identifies the VLAN the frame belongs to as it crosses the trunk.

question: What is the primary purpose of Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) in a switched network?
choices: To load-balance traffic across all redundant links simultaneously
To prevent Layer 2 loops by blocking redundant paths
To assign VLAN membership to switch ports
To translate private IP addresses to public IP addresses
explanation: STP prevents broadcast storms and MAC table instability caused by Layer 2 loops by placing redundant links in a blocking state while keeping one loop-free active path.

question: In Spanning Tree Protocol, which port role is selected on every non-root switch to forward traffic toward the root bridge?
choices: Designated port
Root port
Alternate port
Backup port
explanation: Each non-root switch selects exactly one root port -- the port with the best (lowest cost) path toward the root bridge -- to forward traffic upstream.

question: What is the main benefit of configuring an EtherChannel between two switches?
choices: It bundles multiple physical links into one logical link for increased bandwidth and redundancy without STP blocking any of the bundled ports
It automatically encrypts traffic between the two switches
It converts all bundled ports into access ports
It eliminates the need for VLANs on the link
explanation: EtherChannel bundles multiple physical links into a single logical link, providing combined bandwidth and redundancy. STP treats the bundle as one link, so no member ports are blocked.

question: In a centralized (controller-based) wireless architecture, what is the primary role of the Wireless LAN Controller (WLC)?
choices: To act as a DHCP relay only
To centrally manage configuration, and control access points across the network
To physically connect wireless clients to the switch
To provide wired Layer 2 switching for the access layer
explanation: A WLC centrally manages AP configuration, RF settings, roaming, and security policy for the lightweight access points it controls, simplifying management compared to autonomous APs.

question: Which access point mode allows a lightweight AP to continue switching client traffic locally even if its connection to the wireless LAN controller is lost?
choices: Local mode
FlexConnect mode
Monitor mode
Sniffer mode
explanation: FlexConnect mode allows a lightweight AP to switch client traffic locally and continue providing WLAN service even if its connection to the WLC is lost, unlike local mode which requires the controller for data forwarding decisions.

question: On an 802.1Q trunk link, how is a frame belonging to the native VLAN transmitted?
choices: It is dropped by the switch
It is sent untagged
It is tagged with VLAN ID 0
It is encapsulated in ISL
explanation: Frames belonging to the native VLAN are sent across an 802.1Q trunk without a VLAN tag; both ends of the trunk must agree on which VLAN is native to avoid VLAN hopping issues.
